subject: Request: Early-exit safety net & staged downsell approval for NovaCure deal
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Grant <emily@novacure.com>, Novacure Legal <legal@novacure.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: Early-exit safety net & staged downsell approval for NovaCure deal

Team —

Quick background: NovaCure is moving forward with a 12-month committed plan (reserved capacity + dedicated support) but their board just told them to preserve cash if product-market fit in the POC cohort is slower than expected. They are asking for an early-exit pathway with staged downsell protections and an opt-out trigger tied to defined metrics.

What customer wants (high level):
- Ability to reduce committed throughput by up to 40% after month 3 with a 3-month staged ramp down instead of immediate termination.
- A credit bucket (one-time) to amortize partial refunds during the staged downsell.
- Clear opt-out language: customer gives 60 days’ notice and provides performance evidence (metric set attached).

Why I escalated: this is non-standard on two counts — (1) early exit with downsell (we normally require full notice + pro-rated refunds) and (2) credit bucket size exceeds standard minor concessions. NovaCure is strategic (large logo + potential for expansion in oncology research) and we want to avoid losing them while controlling revenue exposure.

Requested approvals / questions for Deal Desk / Execs:
1) Approve a staged downsell program: allow up to 40% reduction over a 3-month staircase after month 3.
2) Approve a one-time credit bucket up to $75,000 (applied over the staged months) to smooth the transition.
3) Approve revised opt-out language (attached redline) that requires 60 days’ notice and documented failure to meet the agreed-on cohort metrics.
4) Require CS monitoring for 90 days post-downsell and automatic rollback rights if usage rebounds above new floor.

Attachments: NovaCure_MA-Plan_v3.pdf (customer metrics), redwood-proposed-terms-20260901.xlsx (credit math), redline-terms-novacure.docx (proposed contract language).

Asks: Karthik — please weigh in on revenue risk and proposed mitigations. Marissa / Rishi — any executive signoff or counterproposal? Neha — if we approve, CS will need a clear monitoring playbook.

Thanks —
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Emily Grant <emily@novacure.com>, Novacure Legal <legal@novacure.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Early-exit safety net & staged downsell approval for NovaCure deal

On 09/01/2026 09:12, Marcus Lin wrote:
> Team —
>
> Quick background: NovaCure is moving forward with a 12-month committed plan ...

Thanks Marcus — good write-up. A few callouts / clarifying Qs before we route to exec sign-off:

1) Credit size rationale: the $75k bucket needs to be tied to concrete unit economics — can you confirm the expected ARR and token/unit delta if they drop 40%? The spreadsheet helps but please add a per-month P&L line.
2) Minimum floor: instead of allowing a full 40% immediate structural reduction, recommend we require a 30% minimum monthly floor (i.e., we only permit reduction down to 70% of committed) unless legal approves a full 40% carveout tied to a higher credit cap. This reduces tail risk for the quarter.
3) Escrow / amortization: propose credits be held in escrow and applied over the 3-month staircase (not refunded in cash) — standard for committed plan exceptions.
4) Notice window: 60 days is acceptable; prefer 90 days when possible for operational planning. Suggest we compromise at 60 days but require a 30-day notice to CS to begin monitoring playbook.

If you can update the Excel with the ARR impact and a sliding credit schedule, I recommend we approve conditionally at the Deal Desk level (authorize up to $60k credit) and escalate anything above that to Marissa for exec sign-off. Also attach a sample opt-out clause below for legal (I drafted a short form):

"Customer may request a staged reduction in committed units once after month 3, subject to sixty (60) days' prior written notice and the staged reduction schedule in Exhibit A. Credits in lieu of refunds shall be applied to future service charges in equal monthly installments over the staged reduction period and shall not be paid as cash refunds. A minimum monthly usage floor equal to seventy percent (70%) of the committed units shall remain in effect unless otherwise approved in writing by Provider."

Marking to approve conditionally up to $60k pending the updated economics. Marcus — can you get the per-month impact by EOD? If not, we escalate to Marissa for a final call.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Deal Desk, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Novacure Legal <legal@novacure.com>, Emily Grant <emily@novacure.com>, finance@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-02T13:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Early-exit safety net & staged downsell approval for NovaCure deal

Thanks for the details and Karthik's recommendation. I reviewed the attachments and the proposed language. Given NovaCure's strategic opportunity, I approve an exception with the following binding conditions:

1) Staged downsell: approve a stepped reduction up to 40% total, implemented over a maximum of 3 months beginning no earlier than month 4, per the staircase in Exhibit A.
2) Credit bucket cap: authorize a one-time credit bucket not to exceed $65,000 total. Credits will be held as account credit (non-cash) and applied across the staggered months.
3) Minimum floor: a 30% minimum floor must be preserved (i.e., usage cannot fall below 70% of committed units) unless Legal signs off on escalating to a 40% floor reduction with compensating terms.
4) Notice and verification: customer must provide 60 days' written notice and empirical evidence showing cohort KPIs below the agreed threshold. CS must begin active monitoring at notice + 30 days.
5) Contract language: use Karthik's proposed short form in the contract and include explicit rollback rights if usage rebounds above the floor within 90 days. Legal to sign the final redline.
6) Finance/Revenue recognition: finance must sign off on the credit amortization schedule before DocuSign.

I ask Legal to prepare the finalized clause and Finance to confirm the amortization mechanics. Marcus — proceed to get the updated per-month economics into the spreadsheet; once finance confirms we can route DocuSign to procurement (Novacure) for signature. Neha — please prepare the CS monitoring playbook and kickoff timeline once notice is submitted.

This approval is time-limited: if we don't have the finalized contract and finance approval within 10 business days, the exception lapses and we'll revert to standard terms.

Appreciate the quick turnaround on this — close with the customer but make sure all conditions are reflected in the SOW.

Best,
Marissa Cole
VP, Sales — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

"Attachments: redline-terms-novacure.docx, redwood-proposed-terms-20260901.xlsx"
